operating_rules: Four Cs of pricing: Cost (acquisition + sellable state), Customer (target audience lifestyle expectations), Company (brand values unique edge), Competition (positioning understanding)
Pricing Formula: Total Cost x Multiplier + Adjustments = Price (each component tied to the four Cs)
Three-pronged pricing structure: Basic (lowest acceptable price), Advanced (middle, desired option), Expensive (high-end anchor that increases perceived value of middle tier)
Price anchoring tactic: Set anchor price 50% higher than target price. Offer payment plan at original target. Clients accept because anchor reframes perception of middle option as discount
SaaS 10-5-20 rule: 10x value per customer, increase prices by 5% per cohort, push until 20% reject (signals underpricing if rejection is lower)
Airbnb rule set strategy: Use dynamic minimum length of stay based on demand color coding. 5+ dark blue days = 4-day minimum. 7+ consecutive = research why, consider 5-day minimum
Fixed fee model advantage: Removes time-transparency pressure on client. Client pays for output/outcome, not monitored hours. Enables margin padding and profit incentive alignment
Value-based pricing: Calculate client revenue impact from your work. Charge 10-80% of the value created (negotiable). Example: +25% conversion increase = $250k annual lift = $25k fee (10% of value)
Freelancer day-rate evolution: Start with market rate (e.g., $250/day). Increase by $50/day after demonstrating above-average output. Plateau when client market won't sustain higher rates
Proposal research doctrine: Deep client intel (recent podcasts, blog posts, market position) required before sending. Generic proposals fail. Personalization is differentiation
Grant proposal narrative: Lead with statistics/question (attention hook), then specify problem/audience/outcome/partnership rationale. Facts tell, stories sell
Federal proposal evaluation: Look for stated evaluation criteria (price, personnel, management plan, QA, past performance) before drafting. Structure directly to scoring weights
Minimum success criteria first: Define business model goal before product. If $1M/year target, identify all viable paths (licensing, consulting, SaaS, volume product, etc.). Pick one path for focus

specific_tactics: Price anchoring: show fake high price, offer real price as 'discount' to activate loss aversion and perception shift
Two-tier pricing psychology: use payment plans (2k + 2k vs 3k upfront) to make increases feel acceptable
Uneven payment splits: favor front-loaded payments (4k today + 2k later) for cash flow and psychology
Proposal personalization: reference client's recent content, podcasts, market position to demonstrate research
ChatGPT data extraction: export Airbnb CSV payouts, ask AI to identify day occupancy patterns (e.g., 2% Monday occupancy vs 85% avg)
Dynamic minimum length of stay: adjust nightly minimums based on demand signals (dark blue = high demand, extend minimums to capture premium)
Price Labs occupancy prediction: use previous-year occupancy + current booking velocity to forecast future months
Grant proposal hook: lead with local statistic (e.g., '35% of women exiting prison return within 12 months'), then frame nonprofit solution
Freelancer rate increase script: 'I noticed I'm producing 2x output vs peers. Moving forward, my day rate is now $350.'
Fixed fee proposal structure: itemize deliverables but hide hourly math. State terms upfront (3 revisions max, 2-week delay = project close)

contradictions: Cost-based pricing (add margin to cost) vs value-based (10-80% of impact) - segments recommend value-based but practice shows cost+margin still dominates freelance market
Fixed-fee transparency (hide hourly math) vs client trust (visible itemization) - segments show both work depending on client maturity
Raise prices by 5% every 10 customers (SaaS) vs raise only after 20% rejection (market ceiling) - timing conflict unresolved
weird_gold: Herding effect in Airbnb pricing: 70% using same software causes synchronized price moves, creating fake demand signals. Strategy: use occupancy data to move counter-seasonally.
Pricing as product positioning: the price you charge (not the product quality) determines which customer segment you attract. A $2 bottle of water signals premium vs 50-cent signals value.
Payment plan psychology exploit: 4k + 2k feels cheaper than 6k upfront, even though total is identical. Front-loading payment (6 + 3 + 3) makes discount feel compelling without lowering price.

ChatGPT as occupancy forecaster: 'If Monday was 2% occupancy today vs 30% last year, and booking velocity is down, forecast will be 56% of last year's final occupancy' - AI can do occupancy math that Price Labs can't.
Grant funders read budgets first: entire narrative structure is secondary. Lead with budget page design because reviewers scan it before narrative.
Consultant trap: if everyone converts to your pitch, you're underpriced by definition. Wait for 20% rejection or you're leaving 5-10x value on the table.
